name: Chat Message
useWhen: Use this for a short work message in Teams, Slack, or a text.

sections.label: Greeting
sections.what: A short hello with the reader's name. Skip it if you're already talking.
sections.tip: Use their first name, unless they're a boss or customer you don't know well.

sections.label: Main point
sections.what: What you need or what the reader should know, in one or two sentences.
sections.tip: Say the whole point in your first message. Don't send "Hi" and wait for a reply.
sections.good: The Nov 6 client report needs your numbers by 3 p.m.

sections.label: Details
sections.what: Only the facts the reader needs to act: a date, a link, a name.
sections.tip: Keep it short enough to read on a phone. Long news belongs in an email.
sections.good: The file is in the Reports folder. Page 2 is the only part left.
sections.bad: So basically here's the whole backstory on how this all started.

sections.label: Ask
sections.what: The one step you want the reader to take, and by when.
sections.tip: Ask one clear question or give one next step with a time.
sections.good: Can you send them by 3 p.m.?

topics.name: General
dos: Put your whole point in one message
Keep it short enough for a phone
Use a real time or date
donts: Send five messages in a row
Share private news in a group chat

topics.name: Asking a Question
topics.tone: Direct and polite. Make it easy to answer.
dos: Ask the question in your first message
Say when you need the answer

point.tip: Put the question itself first, with what the reader needs to answer it.
point.good: Which version of the Nov 6 report should I send the client?

topics.name: Giving an Update
topics.tone: Calm and clear. News first, then what's next.
dos: Say the news in your first sentence
donts: Bury bad news at the end
Tag everyone when one person needs it

point.tip: Say where the work stands now, in one sentence.
point.good: The client report is done and went out at 2 p.m.
point.bad: So I've been working on things and it's going okay.

topics.name: Running Late or Out
topics.tone: Short and responsible. Say when you'll be there.
dos: Send it the minute you know
Say who is covering, if you can

point.tip: Say you're late or out, and give a real time.
point.good: I'm running late and will be in by 9:30 a.m.
phrases: I'm running late and will be in by [time].
